title: Multiply fractions
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: A whole number times a fraction
sections.objective: Multiply a fraction by a whole number, and find a fraction of an amount.
explain: Don't multiply the bottom too: {6/21} is just {2/7} again.
"{2/3} of 12" is {2/3} × 12: split 12 into 3 groups of 4, take 2 groups: 8.
sections.key: A whole number times a fraction: multiply the top, keep the bottom. The pieces stay the same size; there are just more of them.

sections.title: A fraction times a fraction
sections.objective: Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms.
explain: No common denominator needed (that's for adding), and no multiplying across diagonally.
The picture shows why: the overlap is 8 of the 15 pieces.

visual.caption: Tap the button to shade one fraction, then take the other fraction of it.

sections.key: Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms. A fraction of a fraction is a smaller amount.

worked.note: Tops times tops, bottoms times bottoms.

sections.title: Simplify the product
sections.objective: Write the product in simplest form, or cancel common factors before multiplying.
explain: Multiplying first and simplifying at the end gives the same answer: {3/4} × {2/9} = {6/36} = {1/6}.
sections.key: Simplify the answer, or cancel before you multiply: any top can cancel with any bottom.
sections.workedCaption: Tap through: cancel first, then multiply.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Multiply fractions and whole numbers, and write each answer in simplest form.
sections.key: Whole numbers go over 1. Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms, then simplify (or cancel first).

worked.note: Or as a mixed number, {7 1/2}. Both are fine.

hints.frac.multiply.by-whole: Multiply the top by the whole number and keep the bottom. For "of": divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top.
hints.frac.multiply.by-fraction: Top times top, bottom times bottom.
hints.frac.multiply.simplify: Multiply, then look for a number that divides both the top and the bottom. Or cancel common factors first.
hints.frac.multiply: Write any whole number over 1. Top times top, bottom times bottom, then simplify.

simplifyHint: That's the right amount, but it isn't in simplest form yet. Is there a number that still divides both the top and the bottom?

misconceptionMessages.frac.mult-keep-denominator: When you multiply, the bottoms get multiplied too. Keeping the same bottom is for adding.
misconceptionMessages.frac.mult-cross: It looks like you multiplied across diagonally. For multiplying, it's top times top and bottom times bottom.
misconceptionMessages.frac.mult-added: It looks like you added. This one says ×: multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms.
misconceptionMessages.frac.mult-whole-both: Only the top gets multiplied by the whole number. Multiplying the top and bottom by the same number gives back the fraction you started with.
misconceptionMessages.frac.mult-whole-bottom: Multiply the top by the whole number, not the bottom. 3 × {2/7} is 3 groups of {2/7}: more sevenths, not smaller pieces.
misconceptionMessages.frac.of-divide-only: You found one group. Now take as many groups as the top of the fraction says: multiply by the top.
